title: UniSGR: Unified Framework for Semantic ID Generation and Ranking
summary:
This paper introduces UniSGR, a unified framework designed for semantic ID generation and ranking in recommendation systems, addressing their limitations with multi-stage cascade architectures.

UniSGR employs two stages: first, multi-scenario pre-training on diverse data to learn general skills; second, scenario-specific alignment optimizing Value-Aware Parallel Multi-Token Prediction (VA-PMTP) alongside a unified multi-objective ranking module during joint training.

To improve downstream ranking integration and inference efficiency, UniSGR utilizes Task-Aware Tokens guided by Funnel-Aware Contrastive Learning and an STARK attention mechanism with reorganized KV cache. Extensive offline experiments on a large e-commerce platform confirm its effectiveness and scalability compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval
summary:
Large-scale recommendation systems using two-tower models often struggle with standard negative sampling methods producing easy negatives that don't sufficiently challenge the model.

This paper proposes an LLM-based hard negative sampling technique within clusters. By training an LLM alongside the main system to find semantically similar but distinct items, it generates more difficult examples for comparison during real-time retrieval training.

The method significantly improves recommendation effectiveness by providing challenging information and reducing inherent biases found in typical industry practices.

title: SCOReD: Student-Aware CoT Optimization for Recommendation Distillation
summary:
SCOReD addresses challenges in recommendation system chain-of-thought (CoT) distillation, where standard teacher traces are verbose or poorly fit student models due to high reasoning uncertainty and out-of-distribution issues.

It introduces a framework that parses teacher CoT responses into typed segments and evaluates each segment's importance using the attention scores of the smaller student LLM.

SCOReD dynamically selects edits (keep, rewrite, fuse, prune) for each segment based on answer improvement potential relative to the student model's constraints, leading to optimized traces that improve recommendation performance metrics while reducing reasoning length.
